subject: anaesthesia
title: History of anaesthesia and medical gases

steps.tx: Anaesthesia as a concept was named by **Oliver Wendell Holmes** in 1846, meaning insensibility. The first publicised demonstration of ether general anaesthesia was by **William T. G. Morton** at Boston on 16 October 1846. Earlier, Crawford Long and William Clark used ether without publicising it. Horace Wells and Gardner Colton used nitrous oxide for dental extraction in 1844.

steps.tx: Diethyl ether was the first widely used **inhalational agent** in surgery. It is highly **volatile**, **inflammable** and **explosive**, so **cautery** must never be used near it. It gives good analgesia and marked muscle relaxation, but **induction** is prolonged and **recovery** is slow, with marked nausea. It raises **blood glucose**, so it is avoided in diabetics. Despite these drawbacks it remains in use in low-resource settings because it is cheap.

steps.tx: Medical gas cylinders are colour coded and use a **pin index safety system** so wrong gases cannot be fitted. Oxygen is a black body with white shoulder, pin index 2,5. Nitrous oxide is blue, pin index 3,5. Entonox is blue body with white and blue shoulder, pin index 7. Air is grey with black and white shoulders, pin index 1,5.
steps.say: Medical gas cylinders are colour coded and use a pin index safety system so wrong gases cannot be fitted. Oxygen is a black body with white shoulder, pin index 2,5. Nitrous oxide is blue, pin index 3,5. Entonox is blue body with white and blue shoulder, pin index 7. Air is grey with black and white shoulders, pin index 1,5.

steps.tx: Oxygen cylinders are stored at high pressure, about 2200 psi, and the E cylinder holds about 660 litres. Nitrous oxide is stored as a **liquid** under about 760 psi, so pressure gauge readings do not show remaining content until all liquid has evaporated. Central supplies are housed in a fireproof, ventilated manifold room away from the main hospital building.
